verification.summary: Verification pass 2026-10-29: 21 of 47 figures are confirmed from a direct read of a primary source, 2 remain conflicting and 24 remain unverified. The federal TrumpRx platform, medicare.gov, novocare.com, ozempic.com, aspe.hhs.gov, fda.gov, cms.gov and investor.lilly.com were read directly by request on 2026-10-29, and the Eli Lilly pages were read directly in a browser after the scripted fetches were refused. The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge programme is confirmed at fifty dollars per month. Any figure not marked confirmed still renders no price.
verification.candidateFieldMeaning: Each datum may carry a `candidate` block: the figure research located, with the provenance actually held for it. The engine NEVER reads `candidate`. It exists so /methodology/ can show its work and so a single verification pass can promote a figure with no code change.

lillydirect_self_pay.label: LillyDirect Self Pay
lillydirect_self_pay.description: Eli Lilly's direct-to-patient cash-pay pharmacy. Requires a valid prescription. Bypasses insurance entirely, so the amount paid does not count toward any deductible or out-of-pocket maximum.

novocare_self_pay.label: NovoCare Pharmacy
novocare_self_pay.description: Novo Nordisk's direct-to-patient cash-pay pharmacy. Requires a valid prescription. Bypasses insurance entirely.

trumprx.label: TrumpRx
trumprx.description: Federal direct-purchase platform launched under Most-Favored-Nation pricing agreements with manufacturers. Prices on this platform have moved repeatedly since launch.

copay_card.label: Manufacturer savings card
copay_card.description: A manufacturer copay card used alongside commercial insurance. Universally excludes beneficiaries of federal healthcare programs.

medicare_bridge.label: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge
medicare_bridge.description: A Medicare access pathway reported to provide a fixed monthly beneficiary cost for a covered GLP-1, subject to clinical eligibility criteria.

medicare_part_d.label: Medicare Part D
medicare_part_d.description: Standard Part D coverage where the plan covers the indication. Cost varies by plan, formulary tier and phase of the benefit.

patient_assistance.label: Patient assistance program
patient_assistance.description: Manufacturer-funded assistance for patients below an income threshold. Income-gated and application-based.

list_price.label: List price, no program
list_price.description: The manufacturer's published list price. Shown as the reference point a saving is measured against, not as a pathway to choose.

eligibilityRules.quote: You are not enrolled in any state, federal, or government funded healthcare program, including, without limitation, Medicaid, Medicare, Medicare Part D, Medicare Advantage, Medigap, DoD, VA, TRICARE®/CHAMPUS, or any state prescription drug assistance program;

eligibilityRules.reason: A manufacturer savings card requires commercial insurance. It cannot be used without coverage.
eligibilityRules.quote: If you have been prescribed Zepbound single-dose pen, you must be enrolled in a commercial drug insurance plan;

eligibilityRules.reason: This pathway is available only to Medicare beneficiaries.
eligibilityRules.quote: Medicare will provide access to certain GLP-1 drugs if you’re eligible and have Medicare drug coverage (Part D)

eligibilityRules.reason: Requires a valid prescription from a licensed healthcare provider.
Paying cash bypasses your insurance, so what you spend here does not count toward your deductible or your out-of-pocket maximum.
Paying cash bypasses your insurance, so what you spend here does not count toward your deductible or your out-of-pocket maximum.
Patient assistance programs are income-gated and require an application, usually with proof of income and a prescriber's involvement. Approval is not immediate.
Patient assistance is limited to applicants below an income threshold.
eligibilityRules.basis: Partially evidenced 2026-10-29: the Lilly Cares Foundation pages were read directly and confirm that the programme provides prescribed Lilly medicines free for up to 12 months to qualifying U.S. patients, and the available-medications page is the place a per-medicine eligibility answer lives. The income threshold itself is not published on the pages reached, so the rule is not retired. The denominator is held: the 2026 federal poverty guidelines were read directly on 2026-10-29 (one person: 15,960 dollars for the contiguous states and the District of Columbia).

eligibilityRules.reason: Figures for this pathway were read directly from trumprx.gov on 2026-10-28, so they are no longer hand-curated from an unreachable page. They still carry the date they were read, and prices in this market move without announcement, so check trumprx.gov directly before relying on a price.
Mounjaro is approved for type 2 diabetes, not for weight management. Coverage and program eligibility follow the diabetes indication.
Ozempic is approved for type 2 diabetes, not for weight management. Coverage and program eligibility follow the diabetes indication.

This program is reported to be for beneficiaries who cannot already get a GLP-1 through their Part D plan. A diagnosis of type 2 diabetes, moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea, or noncirrhotic MASH is reported to confer Part D GLP-1 eligibility and therefore to disqualify you from this program, even if you meet every clinical criterion. Confirm your own position with Medicare.
eligibilityRules.quote: You aren't eligible if you: Already get GLP-1 drugs covered through your Medicare Part D plan . Have type 2 diabetes, moderate-to-severe sleep apnea, or fatty liver disease (but your Part D plan might cover your GLP-1s).

eligibilityRules.reason: This programme requires a BMI of 35 or higher, or a BMI of 30 or higher with diastolic heart failure, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or chronic kidney disease at stage 3a or higher, or a BMI of 27 or higher with prediabetes, a previous heart attack or stroke, or peripheral artery disease with symptoms. It covers Foundayo tablets, Wegovy injection and tablets, and the Zepbound KwikPen specifically rather than Zepbound vials, and it is available nationwide. Read from medicare.gov on 2026-10-28.

Medicaid GLP-1 coverage is state-by-state. A federal program reported for 2026 negotiates terms on behalf of state Medicaid agencies, but participation is voluntary and what you pay depends on your own state. There is no national Medicaid price for these medications and this site does not publish one.

IMPORTANT AND UNRESOLVED: sources disagree about whether Medicare and Medicaid beneficiaries may buy through this cash-pay program at all. One reading excludes government-programme beneficiaries outright; another permits anyone with a prescription who chooses to pay cash. We could not settle it, so we are neither hiding this pathway from you nor telling you it is available. Call the program and ask before you rely on it.

This cash-pay pharmacy appears to be open to people who have Medicare or other government coverage but choose to pay cash and not use it. That is a different rule from the manufacturer savings card, which bars government-programme beneficiaries outright. We have not confirmed it directly, so verify before you rely on it.

Patient assistance programmes generally require that you have Medicare or no insurance at all. If you have commercial insurance you are typically not eligible, even if your plan does not cover the medication. Income thresholds also vary by product and we have not confirmed which applies here.

candidate.provenance: Re-checked 2026-10-29: the Zepbound savings card terms were read directly and state three separate figures, each as a bound rather than a price. With commercial insurance that covers the single-dose pen: "pay as little as $25 for a 1-month, 2-month, or 3-month prescription fill", capped at $100 a month and $1,300 a year. With commercial insurance that does NOT cover the pen: "pay as low as $499". For the KwikPen where insurance does not cover it: $299 at 2.5 mg, $399 at 5 mg, $449 at 7.5 mg, and $449 at 10, 12.5 and 15 mg, each capped by a stated maximum monthly saving. Every one of those is "as little as" or "as low as", so none of them is a price and the value stays null. The card also states that it expires and savings end on 12/31/2026.

caveats: The manufacturer states this figure as the price at which it sells to wholesalers, with the wholesale acquisition cost accessed from AnalySource on April 3, 2026. What a patient pays at the pharmacy depends on their insurance, the pharmacy charges, and any assistance available.
A month supply of this product is defined as a once daily 30-day supply.

prices.notes: Direct read of the federal TrumpRx platform, 2026-10-28. The platform states the price per strength and the introductory terms.
caveats: This is an INTRODUCTORY price. The platform states that new patients pay this figure for the first two monthly fills of the 0.25 mg and 0.5 mg strengths, and that the offer runs only between 11/17/2025 and 12/31/2026. Do not budget it as your ongoing cost.

The platform states that after those fills the price is three hundred forty nine dollars per month for the 0.25 mg, 0.5 mg, 1 mg, 1.7 mg and 2.4 mg strengths, and three hundred ninety nine dollars per month for the 7.2 mg Wegovy HD strength. One month is one box of four pens.

prices.notes: Direct read of the federal TrumpRx platform, 2026-10-28. The platform states this figure for the 1 mg, 1.7 mg and 2.4 mg strengths.
caveats: IMPORTANT: the lower figure advertised for this pathway does NOT apply to this dose. It covers only the two starting strengths, and only for the first two monthly fills. At this dose the higher price applies from your FIRST fill, not after a promotional period. Arriving at the counter expecting the advertised figure could mean a difference of roughly 150 dollars on day one. Confirm your dose price before you fill.
The platform also states three hundred ninety nine dollars per month for the 7.2 mg Wegovy HD strength, which is a separate tier from this one.

prices.notes: Standard Part D coverage where your plan covers the indication. There is no single national figure: what you pay depends on your plan, its formulary tier, and which phase of the benefit year you are in.
caveats: Because this depends entirely on your own plan, check your plan formulary directly. Medicare also runs a programme letting you spread drug costs evenly across the year, which can matter more than the monthly figure if your costs are front-loaded.

candidate.provenance: Re-checked 2026-10-28: medicare.gov/drug-coverage-part-d was read directly (it redirects to /health-drug-plans/part-d). It confirms that Part D coverage is provided by insurance companies and that plans decide which drugs are covered, and it introduces the Medicare Prescription Payment Plan. It publishes no price for these medicines, so no value is adopted.
candidate.needs: Not a figure this site can ever publish. The useful additions are the current annual out-of-pocket cap and whether the monthly payment-smoothing programme applies, both from CMS.
